newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rise in crude prices spreads to Japan oil products.
newsitem.headline: Rise in crude prices spreads to Japan oil products.

text.p: Persistent strength in global crude oil prices has forced Japanese refiners to set their November wholesale oil product prices sharply higher than in October, industry officials said on Tuesday.

Refiners Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd, Showa Shell Sekiyu KK and Japan Energy Corp said they had decided to raise their wholesale oil product prices for November by a hefty 1,400 yen ($12) to 1,500 yen ($13) per kilolitre from October.

"If the crude market continues to rise at this pace, the wholesale price for December is likely to be raised by more than 1,000 yen," Idemitsu senior managing director Yasuyuki Yoshida told reporters.

Idemitsu's November wholesale price for gasoline will be 90.20 yen (80 cents) per litre including tax, while kerosene and gas oil, which are not taxed at the wholesale stage, will be priced at 36.2 yen (32 cents) per litre.
The increase in prices reflects a strengthening of crude prices in September combined with the yen's weakness against the dollar, refiners said.
Yoshida said that in September, the average price of Dubai crude -- the benchmark crude in the Asian market -- rose $1.78 per barrel from August to $20.42.
The crude market is continuing to move higher, with the price of Dubai from October 1 to 14 averaging $21.72, he said.
A weakening yen against the dollar also pushed up crude import prices, he said, adding that the yen had eased by about 2.25 yen to the dollar between mid-September and mid-October.

Meanwhile, retail prices have not kept up with the climbing wholesale prices. Cut-throat competition ahead of and after the deregulation of oil product imports in April this year has made retailers loath to raise petrol prices.
Wholesale product prices have risen by 2,500 yen ($22) per kilolitre between August and November, Yoshida said.
However, the national average for the retail price of gasoline as of October 9 was 106 yen (95 cents) per litre, up only one yen (one cent) from the August price, according to industry data.
"We are deeply worried about retail market prices, as they do not seem to be moving in the direction we would like to see," Yoshida said.
Other Japanese refiners are largely expected to raise their November wholesale product prices in line with Idemitsu, Showa Shell and Japan Energy.
In April, major Japanese refiners adopted a wholesale pricing system which reflects the international prices of crude and oil products as well as moves in the currency market.

The system was designed to combat oil product imports following deregulation. Until the liberalisation, only refiners were allowed to import oil products but now, in theory, any company can import them. ($1=112 yen)
